If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, the FootprintSpatialFit is 1. If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, a dwc:footprintSpatialFit is 1. terms.definition: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines the dcterms:Location. A dcterms:Location may have both a point-radius representation (see dwc:decimalLatitude) and a footprint representation, and they may differ from each other.
terms.label: Footprint WKT (IRI)

terms.comments: A dcterms:Location may have both a point-radius representation (see dwc:decimalLatitude) and a footprint representation, and they may differ from each other.
terms.definition: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines a dcterms:Location.
terms.examples: `POLYGON ((10 20, 11 20, 11 21, 10 21, 10 20))` (the one-degree bounding box with opposite corners at longitude=10, latitude=20 and longitude=11, latitude=21)

terms.definition: The full name of the lithostratigraphic formation from which the cataloged item was collected.
terms.label: Formation

terms.definition: The full name of the lithostratigraphic formation from which the dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.
terms.label: Formation

terms.definition: A resource describing a fossilized specimen.
terms.label: Fossil Specimen

terms.definition: A preserved specimen that is a fossil.
terms.examples: `a body fossil`; `a coprolite`; `a gastrolith`; `an ichnofossil`; `a piece of a petrified tree`
terms.label: Fossil Specimen

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI from a controlled vocabulary. A "convenience property" that replaces Darwin Core literal-value terms related to geological context. See Section 2.7.7 of the Darwin Core RDF Guide for details.
terms.definition: Use to link a dwc:GeologicalContext instance to an IRI-identified lithostratigraphic unit at the lowest possible level in a hierarchy.
terms.label: From Lithostratigraphic Unit

terms.comments: Specify the full official name of the funding body. This should include the complete name without abbreviations, unless the abbreviation is an official and commonly recognized form (e.g., NSF for the National Science Foundation). The recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space ( | ).
terms.definition: Text description of organizations or individuals who funded the creation of the resource.
terms.label: Funding Attribution

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An organization or agency that provided funding for a project.
terms.label: Funding Attribution (IRI)

terms.comments: Provide a unique identifier for the funding body, such as an identifier used in governmental or international databases. If no official identifier exists, use a persistent and unique identifier within your organization or dataset. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
terms.definition: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent that financially supported a project.
terms.label: Funding Attribution ID

terms.definition: GenBank Accession number.
terms.label: Gen Bank Num

terms.definition: GenBank Accession number(s) associated with the biological individual(s) referred to by the cataloged object.
terms.label: Gen Bank Number

terms.comments: Examples: "Coordinates generalized from original GPS coordinates to the nearest half degree grid cell", "locality information given only to nearest county".
terms.definition: Actions taken to make the data as shared less specific or complete than in its original form. Suggests that alternative data of highly quality may be available on request.
terms.label: Generalizations

terms.comments: For synonyms the accepted genus and the genus part of the name may be different. The term dwc:genericName should be used together with dwc:specificEpithet to form a binomial and with dwc:infraspecificEpithet to form a trinomial. The term dwc:genericName should only be used for combinations. Uninomials of generic rank do not have a dwc:genericName.
terms.definition: The genus part of the dwc:scientificName without authorship.
terms.examples: `Felis` (for scientificName `Felis concolor`, with accompanying values of `Puma concolor` in acceptedNameUsage and `Puma` in genus)
terms.label: Generic Name

terms.definition: The phylogenetic genus to which the cataloged item belongs.
terms.label: Genus

terms.definition: The name of the genus in which the organism is classified.
terms.label: Genus

terms.definition: The full scientific name of the genus in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
terms.label: Genus

terms.definition: The geodetic datum to which the latitude and longitude refer. If not known, use "not recorded". This concept should be vocabulary-controlled. Example: "WGS84"
terms.label: Geodetic Datum

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI for the EPSG code of the SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use an IRI corresponding to the value `not recorded`.
terms.definition: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude are based.
terms.label: Geodetic Datum (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use the EPSG code of the SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use the value `not recorded`. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for a string literal value.
terms.definition: The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude are based.
terms.label: Geodetic Datum

terms.definition: A set of geological designations, such as stratigraphy, that qualifies a dcterms:Location or source of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
terms.examples: `a particular lithostratigraphic layer`; `a specific chronostratigraphic unit`
terms.label: Geological Context

terms.definition: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:GeologicalContext (the location within a geological context, such as stratigraphy). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
terms.label: Geological Context ID

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An IRI identifying a dcterms:Agent responsible for providing a georeference.
terms.label: Georeferenced By (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A name for a dcterms:Agent responsible for providing a georeference.
terms.label: Georeferenced By

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019.
terms.definition: The date on which the dcterms:Location was georeferenced.
terms.examples: `1963-03-08T14:07-06:00` (8 Mar 1963 at or after 2:07pm and before 2:08pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC); `2009-02-20T08:40Z` (20 February 2009 at or after 8:40am and before 8:41 UTC); `2018-08-29T15:19` (29 August 2018 at or after 3:19pm and before 3:20pm local time); `1809-02-12` (within the day 12 February 1809); `1906-06` (in the month of June 1906); `1971` (in the year 1971); `2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z` (some time within the interval beginning 1 March 2007 at 1pm UTC and before 11 May 2008 at 3:30pm UTC); `1900/1909` (some time within the interval between the beginning of the year 1900 and before the year 1909); `2007-11-13/15` (some time in the interval between the beginning of 13 November 2007 and before 15 November 2007)
terms.label: Georeferenced Date

terms.definition: A reference to the methods used for determining the coordinates and uncertainties. Example: "http://manisnet.org/GeorefGuide.html".
terms.label: Georeference Protocol

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A description or reference to a dwc:Protocol used to determine a spatial footprint, coordinates, and uncertainties.
terms.label: Georeference Protocol (IRI)

terms.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A description or reference to a dwc:Protocol used to determine a spatial footprint, coordinates, and uncertainties.
terms.examples: `Georeferencing Quick Reference Guide (Zermoglio et al. 2020, https://doi.org/10.35035/e09p-h128)`
terms.label: Georeference Protocol

terms.definition: Comments about the spatial description determination, explaining assumptions made in addition or opposition to the those formalized in the method referred to in GeoreferenceProtocol.
terms.label: Georeference Remarks

terms.definition: Comments or notes about the spatial description determination, explaining assumptions made in addition or opposition to the those formalized in the method referred to in dwc:georeferenceProtocol.
terms.label: Georeference Remarks

terms.definition: A list of maps, gazetteers or other resources used to georeference the locality. The content of this concept is meant to be specific enough to allow anyone in the future to use the same resource to georeference the same locality. Examples: "USGS 1:24000 Florence Montana Quad", "Terrametrics 2008 on Google Earth"
terms.label: Georeference Sources

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is describe a georeference with no more than one sampled georeference source. In the case of a georeference that cannot be attributed to a specific source, the recommended best practice is to repeat the property for each IRI that denotes a different source that applies to the georeference. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An IRI for a map, gazetteer, or other resource used to georeference a dcterms:Location.
terms.label: Georeference Sources (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of maps, gazetteers, or other resources used to georeference a dcterms:Location, described specifically enough to allow anyone in the future to use the same resources.
terms.examples: `GeoLocate`; `GeoPick`; `https://www.geonames.org/`; `USGS 1:24000 Florence Montana Quad 1967 | Terrametrics 2008 on Google Earth`
terms.label: Georeference Sources

terms.definition: A categorical description of the extent to which the georeference has been verified to represent the location where the specimen or observation was collected. This element should be vocabulary-controlled. Examples: "requires verification", "verified by collector", "verified by curator".
terms.label: Georeference Verification Status

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A categorical description of the extent to which the georeference has been verified to represent the best possible spatial description for the dcterms:Location of the dwc:Occurrence.
terms.label: Georeference Verification Status (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A categorical description of the extent to which the georeference has been verified to represent the best possible spatial description for the dcterms:Location of the dwc:Occurrence.
terms.examples: `unable to georeference`; `requires georeference`; `requires verification`; `verified by data custodian`; `verified by contributor`
terms.label: Georeference Verification Status

terms.definition: A reference to the methods used for determining the coordinates and uncertainties.
terms.label: Georef Method

terms.definition: A Uniform Resource Name (URN) as a unique identifier for the specimen or observation record. In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one in the form: "[InstitutionCode]:[CollectionCode]: [CatalogNumber]" Examples: 1) urn:lsid:nhm.ku.edu:Herps:32 2) "FMNH:Mammal:145732"
terms.label: Global Unique Identifier

terms.definition: The full name of the lithostratigraphic group from which the cataloged item was collected.
terms.label: Group

terms.definition: The full name of the lithostratigraphic group from which the dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.
terms.label: Group

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.
terms.label: Habitat (IRI)

terms.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.
terms.label: Habitat

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `), with terms in order from the highest taxonomic rank to the lowest.
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of taxa names terminating at the rank immediately superior to the referenced dwc:Taxon.
terms.examples: `Plantae | Tracheophyta | Magnoliopsida | Ranunculales | Ranunculaceae | Ranunculus`; `Animalia`; `Animalia | Chordata | Vertebrata | Mammalia | Theria | Eutheria | Rodentia | Hystricognatha | Hystricognathi | Ctenomyidae | Ctenomyini | Ctenomys`
terms.label: Higher Classification

terms.definition: The combination of all geographic elements less specific than locality. "Like" query operations on this element will search for a substring in any of the higher geography attributes.
terms.label: Higher Geography

terms.definition: The names (concatenated and separated) of geographic elements less specific than the information in the Locality element. "LIKE" or "contains" substring query operations are meant to be used with this element to find matching geographic names. This can be useful if it is unclear in which element a name might be found, and in cases where there is no other appropriate geographic element. Example: "South America, Argentina, Patagonia, Parque Nacional Nahuel Huapi, Neuquén, Los Lagos" with accompanying values "South America" in Continent, "Argentina" in Country, "Neuquén" in StateProvince, and Los Lagos in County.
terms.label: Higher Geography

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `), with terms in order from least specific to most specific.
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of geographic names less specific than the information captured in the dwc:locality term.
terms.examples: `North Atlantic Ocean`; `South America | Argentina | Patagonia | Parque Nacional Nahuel Huapi | Neuquén | Los Lagos` with accompanying values `South America` (continent) `Argentina` (country), `Neuquén` (first order division), and `Los Lagos` (second order division)
terms.label: Higher Geography

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a persistent identifier from a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names.
terms.definition: An identifier for the geographic region within which the dcterms:Location occurred.
terms.examples: `http://vocab.getty.edu/tgn/1002002` (Antártida e Islas del Atlántico Sur, Territorio Nacional de la Tierra del Fuego, Argentina).
terms.label: Higher Geography ID

terms.definition: The combination of names of taxonomic ranks less specific than Genus. "Like" query operations on this element will search for a substring in any of the higher taxon attributes.
terms.label: Higher Taxon

terms.definition: The names of taxonomic ranks less specific than SpecificEpithet concatenated and separated. "LIKE" or "contains" substring query operations are meant to be used with this element to find matching higher taxon names. This element may contain the list of scientific names of all of the supra-specific taxa in the classification used to identify (determine) the specimen or observation. Example: "Animalia, Chordata, Vertebrata, Mammalia, Theria, Eutheria, Rodentia, Hystricognatha, Hystricognathi, Ctenomyidae, Ctenomyini, Ctenomys".
terms.label: Higher Taxon

terms.comments: Example: "Animalia, Chordata, Vertebrata, Mammalia, Theria, Eutheria, Rodentia, Hystricognatha, Hystricognathi, Ctenomyidae, Ctenomyini, Ctenomys".
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of the names for the taxonomic ranks less specific than the ScientificName.
terms.label: Higher Taxon

terms.definition: A unique identifier for the taxon concept less specific than that given in the taxonConceptID.
terms.label: Higher Taxon Concept ID

terms.definition: A global unique identifier for the parent to the taxon.
terms.label: Higher Taxon ID

terms.comments: Example: "Animalia; Chordata; Vertebrata; Mammalia; Theria; Eutheria; Rodentia; Hystricognatha; Hystricognathi; Ctenomyidae; Ctenomyini; Ctenomys"
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of the names for the taxonomic ranks less specific than that given in the scientificName.
terms.label: Higher Taxon Name

terms.definition: A unique identifier for the name of the next higher rank than the scientificName in a taxonomic classification. See higherTaxonName.
terms.label: Higher Taxon Name ID

terms.definition: The full name of the highest possible geological biostratigraphic zone of the stratigraphic horizon from which the cataloged item was collected.
terms.label: Highest Biostratigraphic Zone

terms.definition: The full name of the highest possible geological biostratigraphic zone of the stratigraphic horizon from which the dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.
terms.label: Highest Biostratigraphic Zone

terms.definition: The horizontal geodetic datum to which the DecimalLatitude and DecimalLongitude refer.
terms.label: Horizontal Datum

terms.definition: A resource describing an observation made by one or more people.
terms.label: Human Observation

terms.definition: An output of a human observation process.
terms.examples: `evidence of a dwc:Occurrence taken from field notes or literature`; `a record of a dwc:Occurrence without physical evidence or evidence captured with a machine`
terms.label: Human Observation

terms.comments: For biology, the assignment of a scientific name or taxon concept to a dwc:Organism.
terms.definition: A classification of a resource according to a classification scheme.
terms.examples: `a subspecies determination of an organism`; `a nomenclatural act designating a specimen as a holotype`
terms.label: Identification

terms.comments: Example: "natureOfID=expert identification; identificationEvidence=cytochrome B sequence"
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of additional measurements, facts, characteristics, or assertions about the Identification.
terms.label: Identification Attributes

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
terms.definition: An identifier for a dwc:Identification.
terms.label: Identification ID

terms.definition: Additional information documenting the taxonomic determination of the cataloged item (e.g., "cf.", "aff.", "subspecies in question", etc.).
terms.label: Identification Modifier

terms.definition: A brief phrase or a standard term ("cf.", "aff.") to qualify the identification of the organism when doubts have arisen as to its taxonomic identity (determination). Examples: 1) For the determination "Quercus aff. agrifolia var. oxyadenia", IdentificationQualifier would be "aff. agrifolia var. oxyadenia" with accompanying values "Quercus" in Genus, "agrifolia" in SpecificEpithet, "oxyadenia" in InfraspecificEpithet, and "var." in InfraspecificRank. 2) For the determination "Quercus agrifolia cf. var. oxyadenia", IdentificationQualifier would be "cf. var. oxyadenia " with accompanying values "Quercus" in Genus, "agrifolia" in SpecificEpithet, "oxyadenia" in InfraspecificEpithet, and "var." in InfraspecificRank.
terms.label: Identification Qualifier

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A controlled value to express the determiner's doubts about the dwc:Identification.
terms.label: Identification Qualifier (IRI)

terms.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A brief phrase or a standard term ("cf.", "aff.") to express the determiner's doubts about the dwc:Identification.
terms.examples: `aff. agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (for `Quercus aff. agrifolia var. oxyadenia` with accompanying values `Quercus` in genus, `agrifolia`  in specificEpithet, `oxyadenia`  in infraspecificEpithet, and `var.` in taxonRank); `cf. var. oxyadenia` (for `Quercus agrifolia cf. var. oxyadenia` with accompanying values `Quercus` in genus, `agrifolia` in specificEpithet, `oxyadenia` in infraspecificEpithet, and `var.` in taxonRank)
terms.label: Identification Qualifier

terms.comments: When used in the context of an eco:Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the eco:Survey. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of dcterms:BibliographicResources used in a dwc:Identification.
terms.examples: `Aves del Noroeste Patagonico. Christie et al. 2004.`; `Stebbins, R. Field Guide to Western Reptiles and Amphibians. 3rd Edition. 2003. | Irschick, D.J. and Shaffer, H.B. (1997). The polytypic species revisited: Morphological differentiation among tiger salamanders (Ambystoma tigrinum) (Amphibia: Caudata). Herpetologica, 53(1), 30-49.`
terms.label: Identification References

terms.definition: Comments or notes about the dwc:Identification.
terms.examples: `Distinguished between Anthus correndera and Anthus hellmayri based on the comparative lengths of the uñas.`
terms.label: Identification Remarks

terms.comments: The evidentiary basis, analytical approach, or inferential method by which an identification was determined. Values describe the dominant source of information supporting the identification (e.g., morphology, geography, molecular data, functional attributes, relationships, or taxonomic revision), independent of confidence level or taxonomic outcome. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Identification.
terms.label: Identification Type (IRI)

terms.comments: The evidentiary basis, analytical approach, or inferential method by which an identification was determined. Values describe the dominant source of information supporting the identification (e.g., morphology, geography, molecular data, functional attributes, relationships, or taxonomic revision), independent of confidence level or taxonomic outcome. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Identification.
terms.label: Identification Type

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as that used in HISPID and ABCD. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A categorical indicator of the extent to which a taxonomic determination has been verified to be correct.
terms.label: Identification Verification Status (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as that used in HISPID and ABCD. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A categorical indicator of the extent to which a taxonomic determination has been verified to be correct.
terms.label: Identification Verification Status

terms.definition: The name(s) of the person(s) who applied the currently accepted ScientificName to the cataloged item.
terms.label: Identified By

terms.definition: The name(s) of the person(s) who applied the ScientificName to the object or observation. Example: James L. Patton.
terms.label: Identified By

terms.comments: When used in the context of an eco:Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the eco:Survey. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An IRI identifying a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
terms.label: Identified By (IRI)

terms.comments: When used in the context of an eco:Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the eco:Survey. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A name for a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
terms.examples: `James L. Patton`; `Theodore Pappenfuss | Robert Macey`; `MegaDetector V5`
terms.label: Identified By

terms.comments: When used in the context of an eco:Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the eco:Survey. Recommended best practice is to provide a single identifier that disambiguates the details of the identifying dcterms:Agent. If a list is used, the order of the identifiers on the list should not be assumed to convey any semantics. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
terms.definition: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
terms.examples: `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097` (for an individual); `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097 | https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0098` (for a list of people)
terms.label: Identified By ID

terms.definition: A Universal Resource Locator reference to digital images associated with the specimen or observation.
terms.label: Image URL

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI from a controlled registry. A "convenience property" that replaces literal-value terms related to collections and institutions. See Section 2.7.3 of the Darwin Core RDF Guide for details.
terms.definition: Use to link any subject resource that is part of a collection to the collection containing the resource.
terms.label: In Collection

terms.comments: A string literal name of the dataset can be provided using the term dwc:datasetName. See the Darwin Core RDF Guide for details.
terms.definition: Use to link a subject dataset record to the dataset which contains it.
terms.label: In Dataset

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an IRI from a controlled registry. A "convenience property" that replaces Darwin Core literal-value terms related to locations. See Section 2.7.5 of the Darwin Core RDF Guide for details.
terms.definition: Use to link a dcterms:Location instance subject to the lowest level standardized hierarchically-described resource.
terms.label: In Described Place

terms.definition: The number of individuals present in the lot or container referred to by the catalog number. Not an estimate of abundance or density at the collecting locality.
terms.label: Individual Count

terms.definition: The number of individuals present in the lot or container. Not to be used for observations.
terms.label: Individual Count

terms.definition: The number of individuals present at the time of the dwc:Occurrence.
terms.label: Individual Count

terms.comments: Examples: "U.amer. 44", "Smedley", "Orca J 23"
terms.definition: An identifier for an individual or named group of individual organisms represented in the Occurrence. Meant to accommodate resampling of the same individual or group for monitoring purposes. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to a data set.
terms.label: Individual ID

terms.definition: Brief descriptions of additional information that may exist, but that has not been made public. Information about obtaining the withheld information should be sought from the administrative contact identified in the provider resource metadata (curator, collection manager). Examples: "specific locality information given only to nearest county", "ask about tissue samples", "georeferences given only to nearest degree".
terms.label: Information Withheld

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
terms.label: Information Withheld (IRI)

terms.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
terms.examples: `location information not given for endangered species`; `collector identities withheld | ask about tissue samples`
terms.label: Information Withheld

terms.comments: The term dwc:infragenericEpithet should be used in conjunction with dwc:genericName, dwc:specificEpithet, dwc:infraspecificEpithet, dwc:taxonRank and dwc:scientificNameAuthorship to represent the individual elements of the complete dwc:scientificName. It can be used to indicate the subgenus placement of a species, which in zoology is often given in parentheses. Can also be used to share infrageneric names such as botanical sections (e.g., `Vicia sect. Cracca`).
terms.definition: The infrageneric part of a binomial name at ranks above species but below genus.
terms.label: Infrageneric Epithet

terms.definition: The infraspecific epithet of the scientific name applied to the organism.
terms.label: Infraspecific Epithet

terms.comments: In botany, name strings in literature and identifications may have multiple infraspecific ranks. terms.comments: This term provides context to the dwc:scientificName. Together with the dwc:scientificName, separated by `sensu` or `sec.`, it forms the taxon concept label, which may be seen as having the same relationship to dwc:taxonConceptID as, for example, dwc:acceptedNameUsage has to dwc:acceptedNameUsageID. When not provided, in Taxon Core data sets the dwc:nameAccordingTo can be taken to be the data set. In this case the data set mostly provides sufficient context to infer the delimitation of the taxon and its relationship with other taxa. In Occurrence Core data sets, when not provided, dwc:nameAccordingTo can be an underlying taxonomy of the data set, e.g., Plants of the World Online (http://powo.science.kew.org/) for vascular plant records in iNaturalist (in which case it should be provided), or, which is the case for most dwc:PreservedSpecimen data sets, the dwc:Identification, in which case there is no further context.
terms.definition: The reference to the source in which the specific taxon concept circumscription is defined or implied - traditionally signified by the Latin "sensu" or "sec." (from secundum, meaning "according to"). For taxa that result from identifications, a reference to the keys, monographs, experts and other sources should be given.
terms.examples: `Franz NM, Cardona-Duque J (2013) Description of two new species and phylogenetic reassessment of Perelleschus Wibmer & O’Brien, 1986 (Coleoptera: Curculionidae), with a complete taxonomic concept history of Perelleschus sec. Franz & Cardona-Duque, 2013. Syst Biodivers. 11: 209–236.` (as the full citation of the Franz & Cardona-Duque (2013) in Perelleschus splendida sec. Franz & Cardona-Duque (2013))
terms.label: Name According To

terms.definition: An identifier for the source in which the specific taxon concept circumscription is defined or implied. See dwc:nameAccordingTo.
terms.label: Name According To ID

terms.comments: Example: "http://hdl.handle.net/10199/7"

terms.definition: A resource describing an instance of the Occurrence class.

terms.comments: In Darwin Core, dwc:Organism, dwc:Occurrence, and dwc:MaterialEntity are related, but distinct concepts. A dwc:Organism is a biological individual or group with an identity and life history that persists independently of the particular dwc:MaterialEntities through which it is manifested. A dwc:Occurrence is a dwc:Event that represents the presence or state of a dwc:Organism at a place during an interval of time, with no explicit dependency on any dwc:MaterialEntity. A dwc:MaterialEntity represents physical matter, including whole bodies, parts, or derivatives of dwc:Organisms, that may directly or indirectly serve as evidence of a dwc:Occurrence.
terms.definition: A dwc:Event that establishes the state of a dwc:Organism at a particular place and time.
terms.examples: `a wolf pack on the shore of Kluane Lake in 1988`; `a virus in a plant leaf in the New York Botanical Garden at 15:29 on 2014-10-23`; `a fungus in Central Park in the summer of 1929`; `a male lance-tailed manakin in a courtship display on Isla Boca Brava`

terms.comments: Examples: "Tragus length: 14mm; Weight: 120g", "Height: 1-1.5 meters tall; flowers yellow; uncommon".

terms.comments: Example: "http://mvzarctos.berkeley.edu/guid/MVZ:Mamm:165861"
terms.definition: A reference (publication, URI) to the most detailed information available about the Occurrence.
terms.label: Occurrence Details

terms.comments: In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one from a combination of identifiers in the record that will most closely make the dwc:occurrenceID globally unique.
terms.definition: An identifier for a dwc:Occurrence (as opposed to a particular digital record of a dwc:Occurrence).
terms.label: Occurrence ID

terms.definition: The category of information pertaining to measurements accociated with an occurrence.
terms.label: Occurrence Measurement

terms.comments: Example: "0.01", "normal distribution with variation of 2 m"
terms.definition: The description of the error associated with the occurrenceAttributeValue.
terms.label: Occurrence Measurement Accuracy

terms.comments: Example: "Javier de la Torre"
terms.definition: The agent responsible for having determined the value of the measurement or characteristic of the occurrence.
terms.label: Occurrence Measurement Determined By

terms.comments: Examples: "1963-03-08T14:07-0600" is 8 Mar 1963 2:07pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC, "2009-02-20T08:40Z" is 20 Feb 2009 8:40am UTC, "1809-02-12" is 12 Feb 1809, "1906-06" is Jun 1906, "1971" is just that year, "2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z" is the interval between 1 Mar 2007 1pm UTC and 11 May 2008 3:30pm UTC, "2007-11-13/15" is the interval between 13 Nov 2007 and 15 Nov 2007.

terms.comments: Instances of the dwc:Organism class are intended to facilitate linking one or more dwc:Identification instances to one or more dwc:Occurrence instances. Therefore, things that are typically assigned scientific names (such as viruses, hybrids, and lichens) and aggregates whose dwc:Occurrences are typically recorded (such as packs, clones, and colonies) are included in the scope of this class. In Darwin Core, dwc:Organism, dwc:Occurrence, and dwc:MaterialEntity are related, but distinct concepts. A dwc:Organism is a biological individual or group with an identity and life history that persists independently of the particular dwc:MaterialEntities through which it is manifested. A dwc:Occurrence is a dwc:Event that represents the presence or state of a dwc:Organism at a place during an interval of time, with no explicit dependency on any dwc:MaterialEntity. A dwc:MaterialEntity represents physical matter, including whole bodies, parts, or derivatives of dwc:Organisms, that may directly or indirectly serve as evidence of a dwc:Occurrence.
terms.definition: A particular organism or defined group of organisms considered to be taxonomically homogeneous.
terms.examples: `a specific bird`; `a specific wolf pack`; `a specific instance of a bacterial culture`; `a particular plant gathered in the wild, transplanted to a botanical garden, and preserved as a specimen in a collection`
terms.label: Organism

terms.definition: An identifier for the dwc:Organism instance (as opposed to a particular digital record of the dwc:Organism). May be a globally unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
terms.label: Organism ID

terms.comments: Supports only primary observed interactions, not habitual or derived taxon-level interactions. Pairwise interactions must be used to represent multi-organism interactions. When possible, typify the action rather than the state from which an action is inferred, with the actor as the subject dwc:Occurrence and the acted-upon as the related dwc:Occurrence. Only one direction of a two-way interaction is necessary, though both are permissible as distinct OrganismInteractions with distinct subject dwc:Occurrences.
terms.definition: An interaction between two dwc:Organisms during a dwc:Event.
terms.examples: `a bee visiting a flower`; `a Mallophora ruficauda hunting an Apis mellifera in flight`; `a viral infection in a plant`; `a female spider mating with a male spider`; `a lion cub nursing from its mother`; `a mosquito sucking blood from a chimpanzee's arm`; `a slug eating a fungus growing on decomposing stump (2 interactions)`
terms.label: Organism Interaction

terms.definition: A verbatim description of a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
terms.examples: `Mallophora ruficauda captured an Apis mellifera worker in flight.`
terms.label: Organism Interaction Description

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
terms.definition: An identifier for a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
terms.label: Organism Interaction ID

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
terms.label: Organism Interaction Type (IRI)

terms.definition: Comments or notes about the dwc:Organism instance.
terms.label: Organism Remarks

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term is not intended to be used to specify a type of dwc:Taxon. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term is not intended to be used to specify a type of dwc:Taxon. To describe the kind of dwc:Organism using a URI object in RDF, use rdf:type (http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type) instead.

terms.comments: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known, of the name usage in which the terminal element of the dwc:scientificName was originally established under the rules of the associated dwc:nomenclaturalCode. Unlike basionyms, however, this term can apply to scientific names at all ranks.

The basionym (botany) or basonym (bacteriology) of the dwc:scientificName or the senior/earlier homonym for replaced names.

terms.comments: This term should be used to refer to the dwc:taxonID of a dwc:Taxon record that represents the usage of the terminal element of the dwc:scientificName as originally established under the rules of the associated dwc:nomenclaturalCode. For example, for names governed by the ICNafp, this term would establish the relationship between a record representing a subsequent combination and the record for its corresponding basionym. Unlike basionyms, however, this term can apply to scientific names at all ranks. For Darwin Core Archives the related record should be present locally in the same archive.

terms.definition: An identifier for the name usage (documented meaning of the name according to a source) of the direct, most proximate higher-rank parent taxon (in a classification) of the most specific element of the dwc:scientificName.

terms.definition: A measure of how well the circle defined by the coordinates and uncertainty match the original spatial representation, as a ratio of the area of the circle to the area of the original spatial representation. Legal values are 0, greater than or equal to 1, or undefined. A value of 1 is an exact match or 100% overlap. A value of 0 should be used if the given georeference does not completely contain the original representation. The PointRadiusSpatialFit is undefined if the original representation is a point without uncertainty and the given georeference is not that same point (without uncertainty). If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, the PointRadiusSpatialFit is 1. Detailed explanations with graphical examples can be found in the Guide to Best Practices for Georeferencing (Chapman and Wieczorek, eds. 2006).
terms.label: Point Radius Spatial Fit

terms.comments: Legal values are 0, greater than or equal to 1, or undefined. A value of 1 is an exact match or 100% overlap. A value of 0 should be used if the given point-radius does not completely contain the original representation. The pointRadiusSpatialFit is undefined (and should be left empty) if the original representation is any geometry without area (e.g., a point or polyline) and without uncertainty and the given georeference is not that same geometry (without uncertainty). If both the original and the given georeference are the same point, the pointRadiusSpatialFit is 1. Detailed explanations with graphical examples can be found in the Georeferencing Best Practices, Chapman and Wieczorek, 2020 (https://doi.org/10.15468/doc-gg7h-s853).
terms.definition: A ratio of the area of a point-radius (dwc:decimalLatitude, dwc:decimalLongitude, dwc:coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) to the area of a true (original, or most specific) spatial representation of a dcterms:Location.
terms.label: Point Radius Spatial Fit

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

Referencing a previous Catalog Number does not imply that a record for the referenced item is or is not present in the corresponding catalog, or even that the referenced catalog still exists. This access point is intended to provide a way to retrieve this record by previously used identifier, which may used in the literature. terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

terms.label: Protocol Type

terms.comments: This is a convenience class to group related properties.
terms.definition: Information about an entity’s origins.
terms.label: Provenance

terms.definition: The number of reads obtained for a processed dwc:NucleotideSequence during a dwc:NucleotideAnalysis.
terms.label: Read Count

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A name for a dcterms:Agent responsible for recording a dwc:Occurrence.

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
terms.definition: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for recording a dwc:Occurrence.
terms.examples: `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097` (for an individual); `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097 | https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0098` (for a list of people)

terms.comments: The subject is a dwc:Occurrence and the object is a (possibly IRI-identified) resource that is the field notes.
terms.definition: An identifier given to the dwc:Occurrence at the time it was recorded. Often serves as a link between field notes and a dwc:Occurrence record, such as a specimen collector's number.

terms.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: An identifier given to the dwc:Occurrence at the time it was recorded. Often serves as a link between field notes and a dwc:Occurrence record, such as a specimen collector's number.
terms.label: Record Number

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
terms.definition: An identifier for a dcterms:BibliographicResource.
terms.label: Reference ID

terms.definition: Comments or notes about a dcterms:BibliographicResource.
terms.label: Reference Remarks

terms.comments: From Dublin Core, "This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. This property is an inverse property of Is Referenced By." The intended usage of this term in Darwin Core is to point to the definitive source representation of the resource (e.g.,Taxon, Occurrence, Event in Darwin Core), if one is available. Note that the intended usage of dcterms:bibliographicCitation in Darwin Core, by contrast, is to provide the preferred way to cite the resource itself.
terms.definition: A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.
terms.label: References

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.definition: A category that best matches the nature of a dcterms:BibliographicResource.
terms.label: Reference Type

terms.comments: Example: "PreservedSpecimen"
terms.definition: The nature of the related resource. Recommended best practice is to use the same controlled vocabulary as for basisOfRecord.
terms.label: Related Basis of Record

terms.definition: The fully qualified identifier (Institution Code + " " + Collection Code + " " + Catalog Number) of the related Cataloged Item, preceded by the nature of the relationship (e.g., (sibling of) MVZ Mamm 1234).
terms.label: Related Cataloged Items

terms.definition: One or more GlobalUniqueIdentifiers (cf. http://wiki.tdwg.org/twiki/bin/view/DarwinCore/GlobalUniqueIdentifier ) of related objects or observations, optionally preceded by the nature of the relationship. Examples: "(sibling of) URN:catalog:MVZ:Mammal:1234", "(endoparasite of) URN:catalog:FMNH:Bird:41321", "(sheet 2 of 2) URN:WTU:VascularPlants:353087".
terms.label: Related Cataloged Items

terms.definition: The fully qualified identifier of a related Catalog Item (a reference to another specimen); Institution Code, Collection Code, and Catalog Number of the related Cataloged Item, where a space separates the three subelements.
terms.label: Related Cataloged Item

terms.definition: Free text references to information not delivered via the conceptual schema, including URLs to specimen details, publications, bibliographic references, etc.
terms.label: Related Information

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
terms.definition: An identifier for the related resource (the object) of a dwc:ResourceRelationship.
terms.label: Related Resource ID

terms.comments: Examples: "StillImage", "MovingImage", "Sound", PhysicalObject", "PreservedSpecimen", FossilSpecimen", LivingSpecimen", "HumanObservation", "MachineObservation", "Location", "Taxonomy", "NomeclaturalChecklist", "Publication"
terms.definition: The type of the related resource. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.label: Related Resource Type

terms.definition: The source (person, organization, publication, reference) establishing the relationship between the two resources.
terms.label: Relationship According To

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019.
terms.definition: The date-time on which the relationship between the two resources was established.
terms.examples: `1963-03-08T14:07-06:00` (8 Mar 1963 at or after 2:07pm and before 2:08pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC); `2009-02-20T08:40Z` (20 February 2009 at or after 8:40am and before 8:41 UTC); `2018-08-29T15:19` (29 August 2018 at or after 3:19pm and before 3:20pm local time); `1809-02-12` (within the day 12 February 1809); `1906-06` (in the month of June 1906); `1971` (in the year 1971); `2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z` (some time within the interval beginning 1 March 2007 at 1pm UTC and before 11 May 2008 at 3:30pm UTC); `1900/1909` (some time within the interval between the beginning of the year 1900 and before the year 1909); `2007-11-13/15` (some time in the interval between the beginning of 13 November 2007 and before 15 November 2007)
terms.label: Relationship Established Date

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.definition: The relationship of the subject (identified by dwc:resourceID) to the object (identified by dwc:relatedResourceID).
terms.examples: `same as`; `duplicate of`; `mother of`; `offspring of`; `sibling of`; `parasite of`; `host of`; `valid synonym of`; `located within`; `pollinator of members of taxon`; `pollinated specific plant`; `pollinated by members of taxon`; `on slab with`
terms.label: Relationship Of Resource

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use the identifiers of the terms in a controlled vocabulary, such as the OBO Relation Ontology.
terms.definition: An identifier for the relationship type (predicate) that connects the subject identified by dwc:resourceID to its object identified by dwc:relatedResourceID.
terms.examples: `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002456` (for the relation `pollinated by`); `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002455` (for the relation `pollinates`); `https://www.inaturalist.org/observation_fields/879` (for the relation `eaten by`)
terms.label: Relationship Of Resource ID

terms.definition: Comments or notes about the relationship between the two resources.
terms.examples: `mother and offspring collected from the same nest`; `pollinator captured in the act`
terms.label: Relationship Remarks

terms.definition: A named or coded valued that identifies the kind relationship between this Collection Item and the referenced Collection Item. Named values include: "parasite of", "epiphyte on", "progeny of", etc. In future versions of this schema this attribute should be set-valued.
terms.label: Relationship Type

terms.definition: Free text comments accompanying the cataloged item record.
terms.label: Remarks

terms.definition: Free text comments accompanying the object or observation record.
terms.label: Remarks

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A reproductive condition of a dwc:Organism.
terms.label: Reproductive Condition (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A reproductive condition of a dwc:Organism.
terms.label: Reproductive Condition

terms.definition: An identifier for the resource that is the subject of the relationship.
terms.label: Resource ID

terms.comments: Resources can be thought of as identifiable records or instances of classes and may include, but need not be limited to instances of dwc:Occurrence, dwc:Organism, dwc:MaterialEntity, dwc:Event, dcterms:Location, dwc:GeologicalContext, dwc:Identification, or dwc:Taxon.
terms.definition: A relationship of one rdfs:Resource (http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource) to another.
terms.examples: `an instance of a dwc:Organism is the mother of another instance of a dwc:Organism`; `a uniquely identified dwc:Occurrence represents the same dwc:Occurrence as another uniquely identified dwc:Occurrence`; `a dwc:MaterialEntity is a subsample of another dwc:MaterialEntity`
terms.label: Resource Relationship

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
terms.definition: An identifier for a dwc:ResourceRelationship.
terms.label: Resource Relationship ID

terms.comments: Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights.
terms.definition: Information about rights held in and over the resource.
terms.label: Rights

terms.definition: A person or organization owning or managing rights over the resource.
terms.examples: `The Regents of the University of California`
terms.label: Rights Holder

terms.definition: Container class for information about the results of a sampling event (specimen, observation, etc.)
terms.label: Sample

terms.definition: Container class for information about attributes related to a given sample.
terms.label: Sample Attribute

terms.comments: Example: "0.01", "normal distribution with variation of 2 m"
terms.definition: The description of the error associated with the SampleAttributeValue.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Accuracy

terms.comments: Example: "Javier de la Torre"
terms.definition: The agent responsible for having determined the value of the measurement or characteristic of the sample.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Determined By

terms.comments: Date may be used to express temporal information at any level of granularity. Recommended best practice is to use an encoding scheme, such as the W3CDTF profile of ISO 8601 [W3CDTF].
terms.definition: The date on which the the measurement or characteristic of the sample was made.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Determined Date

terms.comments: Example: "tip of tail missing"
terms.definition: Comments or notes accompanying the measurement or characteristic of the sample.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Remarks

terms.comments: Example: "mm"
terms.definition: The units for the value of the measurement or characteristic of the sample. Recommended best practice is to use International System of Units (SI) units.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Unit

terms.comments: Example: "45"
terms.definition: The value of the measurement or characteristic of the sample.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Value

terms.comments: Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A category or type of substrate sampled during a dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sampled Substrate Category (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary and separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A category or type of substrate sampled during a dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sampled Substrate Category

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is describe a dwc:Event with no more than one sampled substrate layer. In the case of a dwc:Event that cannot be attributed to a specific layer, the recommended best practice is to repeat the property for each IRI that denotes a different layer that applies to the dwc:Event. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An IRI identifying a substrate layer sampled during a dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sampled Substrate Layer (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary and separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of substrate layers sampled during a dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sampled Substrate Layer

terms.comments: Example: "found dead on road"
terms.definition: Comments or notes about the sample or record.
terms.label: Sample Remarks

terms.comments: A dwciri:sampleSizeUnit must have a corresponding dwc:sampleSizeValue. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Ontology of Units of Measure http://www.wurvoc.org/vocabularies/om-1.8/ of SI units, derived units, or other non-SI units accepted for use within the SI.
terms.definition: The unit of measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sampling Size Unit (IRI)

terms.comments: A dwc:sampleSizeUnit must have a corresponding dwc:sampleSizeValue, e.g., `5` for dwc:sampleSizeValue with `m` for dwc:sampleSizeUnit. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: The unit of measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sample Size Unit

terms.comments: A dwc:sampleSizeValue must have a corresponding dwc:sampleSizeUnit.
terms.definition: A numeric value for a measurement of the size (time duration, length, area, or volume) of a sample in a sampling dwc:Event.
terms.label: Sample Size Value

terms.definition: An identifier for the sampling attribute. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
terms.label: Sample Attribute ID

terms.comments: Example: "tail length"
terms.definition: The nature of the measurement or characteristic of the sample. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.label: Sample Attribute Type

terms.definition: The amount of effort expended during a dwc:Event.
terms.examples: `40 trap-nights`; `10 observer-hours`; `10 km by foot`; `30 km by car`
terms.label: Sampling Effort

terms.definition: Container class for information about the conditions and methods of acquisition of samples.
terms.label: Sampling Event

terms.comments: Example: "Relative humidity: 28 %; Temperature: 22 C; Sample size: 10 kg"
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of additional measurements or characteristics of the sampling event.
terms.label: Sampling Event Attributes

terms.definition: An identifier for the sampling event. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
terms.label: Sampling Event ID

terms.comments: Example: "found dead on road"
terms.definition: Comments or notes about the sampling event.
terms.label: Sampling Event Remarks

terms.definition: Container class for information about the location where a sampling event occurred.
terms.label: Sampling Location

terms.comments: Example: "MVZ:LocID:12345"
terms.definition: An identifier for the sampling location. May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
terms.label: Sampling Location ID

terms.comments: Example: "under water since 2005"
terms.definition: Comments or notes about the sampling location.
terms.label: Sampling Location Remarks

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to describe a dwc:Event with no more than one sampling protocol. In the case of a summary dwc:Event in which a specific protocol can not be attributed to specific dwc:Occurrences, the recommended best practice is to repeat the property for each IRI that denotes a different sampling protocol that applies to the dwc:Occurrence.
terms.definition: The methods or protocols used during a dwc:Event, denoted by an IRI.
terms.label: Sampling Protocol (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to describe a dwc:Event with no more than one sampling protocol. In the case of a summary Event with multiple protocols, in which a specific protocol can not be attributed to specific dwc:Occurrences, the recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: The names of, references to, or descriptions of the methods or protocols used during a dwc:Event.
terms.examples: `UV light trap`; `mist net`; `bottom trawl`; `ad hoc observation | point count`; `Penguins from space: faecal stains reveal the location of emperor penguin colonies, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00467.x`; `Takats et al. 2001. Guidelines for Nocturnal Owl Monitoring in North America. Beaverhill Bird Observatory and Bird Studies Canada, Edmonton, Alberta. 32 pp., http://www.bsc-eoc.org/download/Owl.pdf`
terms.label: Sampling Protocol

terms.definition: The full name of lowest level taxon to which the cataloged item can be identified (e.g., genus name, specific epithet, subspecific epithet, etc.).
terms.label: Scientific Name

terms.definition: The full name of the lowest level taxon to which the organism has been identified in the most recent accepted determination, specified as precisely as possible, including name-author, year or authorship, sensu or sec. (according to or following) author, and indication of uncertainty. Conceptually equivalent to a full taxonomic identification as given by the identifier (verbatim). Does not include the identifier name or date of identification. Examples: "Coleoptera" (an Order), "Vespertilionidae" (a Family), "Manis" (a Genus), "Ctenomys sociabilis" (Genus + SpecificEpithet), "Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli" (Genus + SpecificEpithet + SubspecificEpithet), "Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia (Torr.) J.T. Howell" (Genus + SpecificEpithet + InfraspecificRank + InfraspecificEpithet + AuthorYearOfScientificName).
terms.label: Scientific Name

terms.comments: This term should not contain identification qualifications, which should instead be supplied in the IdentificationQualifier term. When applied to an Organism or Occurrence, this term should be used to represent the scientific name that was applied to the associated Organism in accordance with the Taxon to which it was or is currently identified. Names should be compliant to the most recent nomenclatural code. For example, names of hybrids for algae, fungi and plants should follow the rules of the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H.1, H.2 and H.3). Thus, use the multiplication sign `×` (Unicode `U+00D7`, HTML `×`) to identify a hybrid, not `x` or `X`, if possible.
terms.definition: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known. When forming part of a dwc:Identification, this should be the name in lowest level taxonomic rank that can be determined.
terms.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Roptrocerus typographi (Györfi, 1952)` (genus + specificEpithet + scientificNameAuthorship); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia (Torr.) J.T. Howell` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet + scientificNameAuthorship); `×Agropogon littoralis (Sm.) C. E. Hubb.`; `Mentha ×smithiana R. A. Graham`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis (L.) Desf.`
terms.label: Scientific Name

terms.definition: The author of the ScientificName. Can be more than one author in a concatenated string. Should be formatted according to the conventions of the applicable taxonomic discipline.
terms.label: Scientific Name Author

terms.definition: The authorship information for the dwc:scientificName formatted according to the conventions of the applicable dwc:nomenclaturalCode.
terms.label: Scientific Name Authorship

terms.definition: An identifier for the nomenclatural (not taxonomic) details of a scientific name.
terms.label: Scientific Name ID

terms.comments: Examples: "subsp.", "var.", "forma", "species", "genus"
terms.definition: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the scientificName. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.label: Scientific Name Rank

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use IUPAC single character symbols (https://www.bioinformatics.org/sms/iupac.html). Use "N" for an unknown or missing nucleotide, and avoid using "?". The sequence should be written in the 5' to 3' direction.
terms.definition: A string representing nucleotide base pairs.
terms.label: Sequence

terms.definition: The sex of a cataloged item (e.g., male, female, hermaphrodite, gynandromorph, not recorded, indeterminate, transitional - between sexes, for sequential hermaphrodites).
terms.label: Sex

terms.definition: The sex of the biological individual represented by the cataloged object or observation. Examples: "male", "female", "hermaphrodite", "gynandromorph", "monoecious", "dioecious", "not recorded", "indeterminate", "transitional".
terms.label: Sex

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A sex of a dwc:Organism.
terms.label: Sex (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: A sex of a dwc:Organism.
terms.label: Sex

terms.comments: Usually an institutional identifier for a specific named place as opposed to dwc:locationID, which is an identifier for the entire set of distinct information for an instance of dcterms:Location. This term differs from dwciri:fieldNumber in that dwciri:siteNumber is not related strictly to one dwc:Event. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: An identifier for a named site.
terms.label: Site Number (IRI)

terms.comments: Usually an institutional identifier for a specific named place as opposed to dwc:locationID, which is an identifier for the entire set of distinct information for an instance of dcterms:Location. This term differs from dwc:fieldNumber in that dwc:siteNumber is not related strictly to one dwc:Event. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
terms.definition: An identifier for a named site.
terms.label: Site Number

terms.definition: A unique identifier assigned to a material sample (as defined by http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/MaterialSampleID, and as opposed to a particular digital record of a material sample) used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. The identifier can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. The INSDC qualifiers /specimen_voucher, /bio_material, or /culture_collection provide additional context and suggested syntax for this identifier for data submitted to INSDC databases.
terms.label: source material identifiers

terms.definition: The phylogenetic specific epithet of the cataloged item.
terms.label: Species

terms.definition: The specific epithet of the scientific name applied to the organism.
terms.label: Specific Epithet

terms.definition: The name of the first or species epithet of the dwc:scientificName.
terms.label: Specific Epithet

terms.comments: The value is 1 for January 1 and 365 for December 31, except in a leap year, in which case it is 366.
terms.definition: The earliest integer day of the year on which a dwc:Event occurred.
terms.examples: `1` (1 January); `32` (1 February); `366` (31 December); `365` (30 December in a leap year, 31 December in a non-leap year)
terms.label: Start Day Of Year

terms.definition: The time of day when the event began, expressed as decimal hours from midnight, local time.
terms.label: Start Time of Day

terms.definition: The full, unabbreviated name of the state, province, or region (i.e., the next smaller political region than Country) from which the cataloged item was collected.
terms.label: State Province

terms.definition: The full, unabbreviated name of the state, province, or region (i.e., the next smaller political region than Country) in which the organism was collected or observed.
terms.label: State Province

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names. Recommended best practice is to leave this field blank if the dcterms:Location spans multiple entities at this administrative level or if the dcterms:Location might be in one or another of multiple possible entities at this level. Multiplicity and uncertainty of the geographic entity can be captured either in the term dwc:higherGeography or in the term dwc:locality, or both.
terms.definition: The name of the next smaller administrative region than country (state, province, canton, department, region, etc.) in which the dcterms:Location occurs.
terms.label: First Order Division

terms.definition: The full scientific name of the subfamily in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
terms.label: Subfamily

terms.comments: A value for this term should be a complete subgenus name as required by the appropriate nomenclatural code.
terms.definition: The full scientific name of the subgenus in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
terms.label: Subgenus

terms.definition: The phylogenetic subspecific epithet of the cataloged item.
terms.label: Subspecies

terms.definition: The full scientific name of the subtribe in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
terms.label: Subtribe

terms.comments: A taxonomic category subordinate to an order and superior to a family. According to ICZN article 29.2, the suffix `-oidea` is used for a superfamily name.
terms.definition: The full scientific name of the superfamily in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
terms.label: Superfamily

terms.definition: A resource describing an instance of the Taxon class.
terms.label: Taxon

terms.definition: A group of organisms (sensu http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0100026) considered by taxonomists to form a homogeneous unit.
terms.examples: `the genus Truncorotaloides as published by Brönnimann et al. in 1953 in the Journal of Paleontology Vol. 27(6) p. 817-820`
terms.label: Taxon

terms.definition: Information about the authorship of this taxon concept which uses the scientificName in their sense (secundum, sensu). Could be a publication (identification key), institution or team of individuals.
terms.label: Taxon According To

terms.comments: Example: "iucnstatus=vulnerable; distribution=Neuquen, Argentina"
terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of additional measurements, facts, characteristics, or assertions about the taxon.
terms.label: Taxon Attributes

terms.definition: An identifier for the taxonomic concept to which the record refers - not for the nomenclatural details of a dwc:Taxon.
terms.label: Taxon Concept ID

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. Terms in the dwciri: namespace are intended to be used in RDF with non-literal objects.
terms.definition: A pattern to use to construct a dwc:Identification from dwc:Taxon names and identification qualifiers.
terms.label: Taxon Formula (IRI)

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.definition: A string representing the pattern to use to construct a dwc:Identification from dwc:Taxon names and identification qualifiers.
terms.examples: `A`; `not A`; `A ?`; `A or B`; `A and B`; `A x B`; `A cf.`; `A aff.`
terms.label: Taxon Formula

terms.definition: A global unique identifier for the taxon (name in a classification).
terms.label: Taxon ID

terms.definition: An identifier for a dwc:Taxon.
terms.label: Taxon ID

terms.definition: A unique identifier for the scientificName.
terms.label: Taxon Name ID

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
terms.definition: The status of the use of the dwc:scientificName as a label for a taxon. Requires taxonomic opinion to define the scope of a dwc:Taxon. Rules of priority then are used to define the taxonomic status of the nomenclature contained in that scope, combined with the experts opinion. It must be linked to a specific taxonomic reference that defines the concept.
terms.label: Taxonomic Status

terms.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).
terms.definition: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.
terms.label: Taxon Rank

terms.definition: Comments or notes about the taxon or name.
terms.examples: `this name is a misspelling in common use`

terms.definition: A list (concatenated and separated) of nomenclatural types (type status, typified scientific name, publication) applied to the subject.

terms.comments: The content of this term should include no embellishments, prefixes, headers or other additions made to the text. Abbreviations must not be expanded and supposed misspellings must not be corrected. Lines or breakpoints between blocks of text that could be verified by seeing the original labels or images of them may be used. Examples of material entities include preserved specimens, fossil specimens, and material samples. Best practice is to use UTF-8 for all characters. Best practice is to add comment “verbatimLabel derived from human transcription” in dwc:materialEntityRemarks. Examples can be found at https://dwc.tdwg.org/examples/verbatimLabel.
terms.definition: A verbatim original representation of the written information affixed or related to a dwc:MaterialEntity.
